scope: Independent counterexample-route sources only; primary mathematical sources. No external communication.

sources.title: On quasiconvex subgroups of word hyperbolic groups
sources.supports: An infinite-index quasiconvex subgroup of a torsion-free non-elementary hyperbolic group lies in a quasiconvex free product H*Z.

sources.authors: F. Haglund and D. T. Wise
sources.title: Special cube complexes
sources.locator: Theorem 7.3 and canonical completion/retraction proof; original theorem referenced in W12
sources.supports: Quasiconvex subgroups of hyperbolic virtually compact special groups are virtual retracts.

sources.title: The structure of groups with a quasiconvex hierarchy
sources.locator: Abstract and special-complex canonical completion/retraction material
sources.supports: Author-hosted primary text explicitly states every quasiconvex subgroup of the hyperbolic hierarchy groups is a virtual retract.

sources.title: Outer Limits
sources.supports: The map a->b,b->c,c->ab is a stable expanding train track without periodic Nielsen paths.

sources.title: Hyperbolic automorphisms of free groups
sources.supports: Atoroidal free-group automorphisms have word-hyperbolic mapping tori.

sources.authors: M. F. Hagen and D. T. Wise
sources.title: Cubulating hyperbolic free-by-cyclic groups: the general case
sources.supports: Every hyperbolic finite-rank free-by-cyclic group acts freely and cocompactly on a CAT(0) cube complex.

sources.authors: I. Agol, with appendix by Agol, D. Groves and J. Manning
sources.title: The virtual Haken conjecture
sources.supports: Cubulated hyperbolic groups are virtually special.

sources.authors: N. Bergeron, F. Haglund and D. T. Wise
sources.title: Hyperplane sections in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds
sources.locator: Published abstract and standard arithmetic-group virtual retraction results; early author manuscript https://www.math.u-psud.fr/~haglund/BHW%2828-11-08%29.pdf
sources.supports: Standard arithmetic hyperbolic manifold groups virtually retract onto geometrically finite subgroups.

sources.authors: G. Avramidi, B. Okun and K. Schreve
sources.title: Homology growth, hyperbolization, and fibering
sources.supports: Uniform arithmetic lattices in real hyperbolic space of simplest type are virtually special; records relevant higher-dimensional examples.

sources.title: Totally Geodesic Spectra of Arithmetic Hyperbolic Spaces
sources.supports: Quadratic subforms yield totally geodesic arithmetic subspaces.

sources.title: Surface subgroups of graph products of groups
sources.locator: Abstract and graph-product virtual compact specialness theorem
sources.supports: Graph products of finite or cyclic groups are virtually cocompact special, covering all finite-graph RACGs.

sources.authors: F. Haglund and D. T. Wise
sources.title: Coxeter groups are virtually special
sources.supports: Every finitely generated Coxeter group is virtually special; RACG compactness also follows from K12.

sources.title: The geometry and topology of Coxeter groups
sources.locator: Proposition 8.8.5 (virtual freeness); Theorem 12.6.1 and Corollary 12.6.3 (Moussong); Example 14.2.2 (polygon groups)
sources.supports: Original-author monograph records the Coxeter structural criteria used in the elementary RACG argument.

sources.title: Surface groups among cubulated hyperbolic and one-relator groups
sources.locator: Current author preprint; v2 html https://arxiv.org/html/2406.02121v2 Theorem A
sources.supports: A cubulated hyperbolic group unless free/surface has an infinite-index one-ended quasiconvex subgroup. This does not by itself prove that subgroup has nonzero virtual H2; included to identify exact gap.
